sharedimp

sharedimp is an R implementation of the linear-regression variant of ultra-marginal feature importance (UMFI-LR; Janssen, Guan & Robeva, AISTATS 2023) designed for modern, resampling-based machine-learning workflows. It is a companion to the Python package of the same name (sharedimp-py); both follow the specification in docs/specification.md.

We do not claim a new importance measure. The package makes an existing one safe and convenient:

  • fold-internal residualization: the OLS coefficients used to remove the anchor’s linear component from the other features are estimated on the training rows of each fold and applied, unchanged, to the assessment rows;
  • paired full/reduced evaluation: the model with the anchor and the model without it are evaluated on the same assessment rows, fold by fold;
  • metric-independent sign: importance is positive whenever keeping the anchor predicts better, for metrics to maximize and to minimize alike;
  • no truncation: negative values are reported, not clipped to zero;
  • tidymodels adapters: parsnip learners, rsample resamples and yardstick metrics, with fixed hyperparameters and a seed argument;
  • per-fold results are always retained.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dsc-chiba-u/sharedimp-r")

Docker

A ready-to-use image with R, sharedimp and its dependencies is published from the main branch to GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub. Both registries receive the same build; tags are latest (last successful build of main) and the short commit SHA.

docker pull ghcr.io/dsc-chiba-u/sharedimp-r:latest   # or koki/sharedimp-r:latest
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/dsc-chiba-u/sharedimp-r:latest           # interactive R
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/dsc-chiba-u/sharedimp-r:latest Rscript analysis.R

The image is based on rocker/r-ver (a pinned stable R release) and is built by .github/workflows/build_test_push.yml; the build installs the package, runs its full test suite and a smoke test (docker/smoke-test.R) inside the image and fails if any of them fails. Pull requests only build and test; nothing is pushed. To build locally:

docker build -t sharedimp-r .
docker run --rm sharedimp-r Rscript -e 'library(sharedimp); example(shared_importance)'

Usage 

library(sharedimp)
set.seed(1)
n <- 300
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n), x4 = rnorm(n))
x$x5 <- x$x1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)        # a noisy copy of x1
y <- 3 * x$x1 + 2 * x$x2 + x$x3 + rnorm(n)

# Default: random forest (ranger, 500 trees), 5-fold CV, MSE
res <- shared_importance(x, y, seed = 1)
res
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       regression
#>   learner:    rand_forest
#>   metric:     mse (minimize); score = -mse, importance = score_full - score_reduced
#>   resampling: 5-fold cross-validation (1 repeat)
#>
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   feature importance importance_std score_full score_reduced n_splits
#>   ...

# Fast deterministic linear learner, explicit metric (r2 = 1 - SS_res / SS_tot)
shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", metric = "r2", v = 5, seed = 1)

# Per-split paired scores (common schema with the Python package)
fold_results(res)

# Classification (first level = event level), any yardstick metric
yb <- factor(y > median(y), labels = c("low", "high"))
shared_importance(x, yb, metric = "roc_auc", seed = 1)

# Any parsnip specification with fixed hyperparameters (here: lasso via glmnet)
spec <- parsnip::linear_reg(penalty = 0.01, mixture = 1) |>
  parsnip::set_engine("glmnet")
shared_importance(x, y, learner = spec, seed = 1)

See vignette("sharedimp") for a longer walk-through.

How it works

For each anchor feature i and each split:

  1. On the training rows, regress every other feature on the anchor (X_j = a_j + b_j X_i + e) and residualize both training and assessment rows with the same (a_j, b_j). A column that is an exact affine function of the anchor gets a residual of exactly zero (and is kept).
  2. Fit the learner to the full representation (the anchor, raw and in its original position, plus the residualized others) and to the reduced representation (the residualized others only).
  3. Score both on the assessment rows, with scores oriented greater-is-better (-mse, -log_loss, r2, accuracy, …), and take importance = score_full - score_reduced.
  4. Average over splits; keep the split-level table.

The R and Python packages share one specification (docs/specification.md) and produce identical tables on deterministic learners with explicit splits.

What the numbers are not

They are out-of-sample predictive gains for a particular learner, metric and resampling scheme. They are not causal effects, conditional effects or regression coefficients, and the package provides no confidence intervals or p-values; importance_std is a descriptive between-split dispersion.

Differences from the reference UMFI-LR implementation

aspect HydroML/UMFI sharedimp
residualization fit whole data set training fold only
gate slope p-value < 0.01 always residualize
evaluation ranger out-of-bag R² / accuracy with floors paired per-fold metrics, any learner
negative values set to 0 kept
learner / metric fixed (ranger 100 trees; R², accuracy) configurable, fixed hyperparameters

Details and a recorded numerical comparison: docs/specification.md, docs/umfi_comparison.md.

Reference

Janssen, J., Guan, V., & Robeva, E. (2023). Ultra-marginal Feature Importance: Learning from Data with Causal Guarantees. Proceedings of the 26th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), PMLR 206:10782–10814. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/janssen23a.html
